title: a-marked-envelope-goes-back-to-its-sender
intention: Every device shim returns a body carrying a return-kind testing mark to its sender, unacted on, before any device code runs, so a test's arrival at a device is answered by the return itself.
why: Akien's re-plan 2026-10-05 (/home/akien/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md 8e): a test's message that lands at a device is valid mail, but the device need not act on it — its shim returns it to the tester, the return is the 'got here', and the tester marks the test complete. Where: 'the shim. device gets the "perform this test" kind later'. The lived symptom today is test mail sitting in device inboxes (603 envelopes measured) and devices acting on fixtures; with the return, a device never sees a test's mail and the tester gets a definite answer instead of a timeout. RULE 1: the return lives in the base tool, so no device code changes.
traces_to: Test against live, marked as testing (ruled 2026-09-28, extended 2026-10-04: consumers tolerate testing artifacts; reshaped 2026-10-05 to return-to-sender at the shim); RULE 1 (the return lives in the base tool and no device code is touched); Law 4 (every shim returns by construction, not by each device remembering); ticket 71d1bbfa98b0
how: In cairn/tools/base/shim.py: BaseShim._return_if_marked(envelope) reads cairn.tools.base.testing_mark.mark_of(body); a return-kind mark posts {testing: mark, is_return: True, original_verb, original_addressee} to the envelope's sender on the personal channel with reply_to = the envelope id, and deliver() returns {returned: True, test, to} without starting the device; a body already flagged is_return goes to a new handle_return() (base: emit test_returned, post nothing) so a return is never returned again; any other kind passes through. BaseShim.__init_subclass__ wraps a subclass's own deliver() so the return runs first even where the override never calls the base (cc_0, codemother verbless mail, tester replies). _clear_mail_troubles treats a returned envelope as no take. Proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_marked_envelope_goes_back_to_its_sender.py, written red.
falsifier: GREEN when cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_marked_envelope_goes_back_to_its_sender.py passes all four teeth against a spy bus: (1) a return-marked envelope is posted back to its sender exactly once, reply_to its id, the mark carried in the body with is_return True, the device never started and no verb handler run; (2) a subclass whose own deliver() never calls the base still returns it, and the override body never runs; (3) an unmarked envelope and a well-formed perform-kind mark both reach the device's verb handler with no return posted; (4) an is_return envelope is not posted again, wakes no device, emits test_returned, and clears no mail trouble through _clear_mail_troubles; and cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_shim.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_bounce_answers_the_request_that_bore_it.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_bounce_raises_the_mail_trouble.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_unread_mail_is_not_kept.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_the_testing_mark_carries_a_kind.py, cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_cc_device.py stay green. RED if any fails. Wrong intent if a return must route somewhere other than the envelope's sender (then the mark carries its return address).

decisions.text: D1: SETTLED: apply exactly the unified diff carried in this ticket's build_patch field (`git apply` from a file holding that text, run in the cairn repo root). It changes only cairn/tools/base/shim.py: imports cairn.tools.base.testing_mark, adds BaseShim.__init_subclass__ (wraps a subclass's own deliver so _return_if_marked runs first), _return_if_marked and handle_return, calls _return_if_marked at the top of BaseShim.deliver, and makes _clear_mail_troubles skip a taken result with returned True. No other code changes; no device shim is edited.

D2: SETTLED: the proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_marked_envelope_goes_back_to_its_sender.py is already on disk, written red (teeth 1, 2 and 4 fail before the build; tooth 3 guards unchanged behaviour and passes). After the build it prints four PASS and exits 0; the regression proofs cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_shim.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_bounce_answers_the_request_that_bore_it.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_bounce_raises_the_mail_trouble.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_unread_mail_is_not_kept.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_the_testing_mark_carries_a_kind.py, cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_cc_device.py each exit 0.
